title: Payer Frequency Edits and the 30-Day Blocks of a Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program Sensor Refill
content:
Benefits verification bulletin — Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program.

The payer's frequency edit decides which 30-day blocks of a sensor refill (A4239) delivery are at risk of non-payment because the supply the payer already paid for on the latest refill has not yet run out; it measures that against the paid-supply end, the day on which the supply the payer paid for on the latest refill is reckoned to end. It applies to a refill on a tier where each refill requires the customer's own confirmation (CGM Commercial HMO Program, CGM Commercial PPO Program, CGM Medicare Advantage Program, CGM Original Medicare Program, CGM Medicaid Program) that draws on the authorization grant resting on the newest written order of the item.

## The edit

The payer's frequency edit replaces which blocks of the delivery are at risk against the paid-supply end, by these rules, reading the claim that billed the latest refill (the latest claim submitted for the item's refill shipment with the latest ship date) and the payer remittances posted for that claim:

1. When the payer paid any amount on the latest refill's claim — a remittance for that claim has posted and the payer-paid amounts on its remittances total more than zero — every 30-day block of the delivery that begins before the paid-supply end is at risk.
2. When a remittance for that claim posted with no payer payment — the payer-paid amounts on its remittances total zero — only the delivery's first block is at risk, and only when the paid-supply end is after today.
3. Otherwise — no remittance for that claim has posted, or the latest refill was never claimed — the standard at-risk blocks apply: every 30-day block of the delivery is at risk when the paid-supply end is after today, and no block is at risk when the paid-supply end is today or earlier.

The delivery's blocks are counted from today: the first begins today, the second 30 days later, and so on. Under rule 1 the number of blocks at risk is the calendar days from today to the paid-supply end, divided by 30 and rounded up to a whole block, none when the paid-supply end is not after today, and never more than the delivery's blocks.

## Input, judgement, result (hypothetical dates; today is a hypothetical 1 March; a three-block delivery)

| Remittance for the latest refill's claim | Paid-supply end | Blocks at risk |
|---|---|---|
| payer paid any amount | 15 April (45 days ahead) | 2 — blocks beginning 1 March and 31 March; the third begins 30 April, after the end |
| payer paid any amount | 31 March (30 days ahead) | 1 — the second block begins on 31 March itself, not before the end |
| payer paid any amount | 2 March (1 day ahead) | 1 |
| payer paid any amount | 1 March or earlier | none |
| payer paid any amount | 15 June (106 days ahead) | 3 — capped at the delivery's three blocks |
| posted, payer paid nothing | 15 April | 1 — the first block only |
| posted, payer paid nothing | 1 March or earlier | none |
| none posted, or never claimed | 15 April | 3 — every block of the delivery |
| none posted, or never claimed | 1 March or earlier | none |

## Points of judgement

- Only remittances that answer the claim for the latest refill are read; remittances for older shipments do not decide the rule.
- Rule 1 and rule 2 differ only in the payer-paid total on those remittances: any amount above zero puts the delivery under rule 1.
- Rule 2 and rule 3 differ in whether a remittance answering that claim has posted at all: a posted remittance with no payer payment limits the risk to the first block, while with none posted the whole delivery is at risk.
